 Sedgwick County DA announces driver in Stryker crash will not face charges; no evidence that act was intentional 
 By Matt Heilman and Jeffrey Lutz Published : Nov. 12, 2026 at 12:36 PM CST | Updated : 1 hour ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google WICHITA, Kan. (KWCH) - Update: Sedgwick County district attorney Marc Bennett announced the driver of the pickup that struck and killed two people and injured 10 others at Stryker Complex last month will not face charges.
 Bennett and Wichita police chief Joe Sullivan provided an update on the investigation into the incident, offering several details about how the investigation unfolded and the key pieces of evidence considered.
 Sullivan said they met with the families of the victims privately before publicly announcing the decision. Nick Schafer, 35, and 6-year-old Cole Adrian, both of McPherson, were killed in the crash.
 The driver drove to Stryker from Garden City with her children, who played soccer at Stryker that day. The driver was not identified.
 Bennett said she reported that the pickup was not her usual vehicle. She was sleeping in the vehicle just prior to the crash and believed she had put the pickup into park.
 While she was either asleep or falling asleep, one of her children put the sunshades up. Soon after, the pickup jumped the curb and went onto the field of play.
 Bennett said he considered six possibilities as reasons for the crash:
 A medical emergency 
 Impairment or intoxication 
 A vehicle mechanical malfunction 
 An intentional act 
 One of the children or the woman, while she slept, inadvertently put the vehicle into drive 
 As the driver pulled up to the curb, she was confused about the gear the car was in 
 Bennett ruled out the first five possibilities. He said he did not reach a conclusion about the sixth. He said for charges to be filed, the act had to be intentional, knowing and/or reckless.
 Bennett determined that not only was there not evidence that the act was not intentional, but in fact there was evidence that it was not done on purpose.
 “This is not a crime, and I cannot charge this driver with a crime,” Bennett said.
 Bennett said that though the crash may have appeared to be an act of negligence, negligent homicide is not a chargeable offense in Kansas. He said that the incident did not meet the standards for vehicular homicide, a misdemeanor in Kansas.
 The woman said the woman had no confrontations at Stryker that day. She hysterically expressed regret following the incident.
 Police reviewed 60 videos and 41 emergency calls, interviewing more than 100 witnesses.
 One of the first witnesses who communicated with the driver was an off-duty law enforcement officer. That officer recorded the interaction.
 To determine the driver’s condition, a blood sample was taken. There were no impairing substances in the blood. The driver’s medical records were also subpoenaed. 
 Bennett said the philosophy going into the investigation was to “know everything that was knowable.”
 Sullivan said medical records and videos offered no evidence that the driver was impaired.
 “My mind went to the worst-case scenario,” Bennett said of when he first heard about the incident.
 Bennett said he was not alone in that assumption, and that one witness thought they would need to use a gun to subdue the driver.
 Police obtained a vehicle history and checked for recalls, of which none were found.
 “Every lead was examined. Every piece of evidence was reviewed,” Sullivan said.
 No mechanical issues were found to the vehicle. Sullivan said that if the vehicle had been left in park, it would not have been able to to clear a curb that enabled it to approach the soccer fields.
 That left questions about the exact circumstances behind who put the vehicle into drive and when and how it was shifted.
 “There are some questions that we may never be able to answer with complete certainty,” Sullivan said.
 The Sedgwick County District Attorney’s Office and the Wichita Police Department are holding a press conference at 3:45 p.m. to provide an update on the investigation into the Oct. 17 deadly crash at the Stryker Sports Complex. 
 Sedgwick County District Attorney Marc Bennett and WPD Chief Joe Sullivan are among those expected to speak at the press conference. 
 Following the incident in which two people died and 10 others were injured after a pickup truck was driven onto a soccer field, the driver hasn’t been charged as the investigation carries on. 
 As of late October, police said they were waiting for toxicology reports and vehicle examination to be completed before moving forward. The circumstances leading up to the crash are still unknown, and as such, it’s unclear if charges will be filed in the case. 
 The Sedgwick County DA’s Office did not specify whether a possible decision on charges would come with Thursday’s press conference. We will stream that event live in this story and will relay any new information that comes out of the press conference.
